text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: spike in 5xx and 429 across api-prod-eu cluster. Error rate (5xx) > 8% over last 5m, 429 rate > 12%. Possible cascading throttles. See summary: https://monitoring.redwood.example/alerts/1792003456

maya-oncall: Ack. I'm paged, joining. Paging @ben-sre and @sam-night for SRE support.

ben-sre: On it. grabbing logs and recent deploys. When did the spike start?

maya-oncall: First uptick at 2026-03-14T22:24:10Z. I see a config change to rate-limits pushed ~22:22 by jordan-dev.

jordan-dev: I rolled out a quota tweak to global quota policy to tighten burst limits on /v1/generate as part of cost-savings. Deployed at 22:21:58 (canary -> 100%). I didn't see errors during canary.

ben-sre: Ok that matches. I'm seeing Envoy upstream 429s for backend service "inference-router" and then downstream 502/504 coming from the gateway when it hits connection drains. Logs:```
[22:24:12] envoy: upstream_response_time=0.002 code=429 cluster=inference-router
[22:24:13] gateway: backend_timeout id=rt-12 svc=inference-router status=504
[22:24:15] app: seq=1234 error=upstream_5xx code=502
```

maya-oncall: This looks like quota misapply -> backpressure -> connection exhaustion -> 5xx cascade. Need immediate mitigation: rollback rate-limit change and open emergency higher quota on critical routes.

ben-sre: Agreed. I'm going to revert the rate-limit config to previous commit. @jordan-dev can you hold any config pushes?

jordan-dev: Hold in place, disabling further rollouts. I can trigger rollback now.

ben-sre: Rolling back to commit abcdef (pre-change). Command:```
kubectl -n infra apply -f /deploy/rate-limits/rollback-abcdef.yaml
# watch
kubectl -n infra rollout status configmap/rate-limits
```

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job started by ben-sre at 22:28:01Z.

maya-oncall: I'm enabling emergency bypass for critical customers and increasing quota for internal api-key (prod-critical) to prevent immediate 429s:```
# temporary policy
apiVersion: v1
kind: Policy
metadata:
  name: emergency-bypass
spec:
  allow:list: ["prod-critical"]
  rate: "unlimited"
```

luis-cs: Heads-up: we have a few enterprise users actively seeing errors. I'll prep a short CS status message once we have rollback confirmation.

sam-night: Monitoring token-level metrics, I can rake down bad client flows if needed. Also enabling additional worker pods to absorb bursts (scale +2).```
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/inference-router --replicas=12
```

ben-sre: Rollback finished at 22:30:05Z. Configmap reverted. I'm seeing 429 drop from 12% -> 3% over the next 60s. 5xx also trending down.

incident-bot: Alert resolved? Current 5xx=1.2% 429=2.8% over 5m. Incident severity reduced to P2.

maya-oncall: Confirming stability. Keeping emergency bypass for 10 more minutes then remove if stable. Preparing postmortem notes.

luis-cs: Draft for customers: "We experienced an availability impact between ~22:24 and ~22:31 UTC due to an unintended rate-limit configuration change that caused cascading 429/5xx responses. The change was rolled back and service restored. We're investigating root cause and mitigation steps." OK to send after final checks?

maya-oncall: Fine to send after we remove bypass and verify 15m. Add: affected customers, timeframe, mitigation, and follow-up.

jordan-dev: Going to add a safety gate to deploy pipeline to prevent global quota changes from auto-promoting to 100% without additional smoke tests. I'll open a PR.

ben-sre: Follow-up actions: 1) PR for deploy gate (jordan-dev) 2) Add alert suppression windows for planned quota changes 3) Add circuit-breaker to prevent backend connection exhaustion 4) Postmortem (maya-oncall)

sam-night: Handing off monitoring and follow-up to night rotation (@sam-night). I'm available on pager for next 2 hours.

luis-cs: Sent customer note to impacted accounts (initial). I'll add a follow-up with more details once postmortem is done.

maya-oncall: Closing the paging loop. Thanks everyone. Filing incident ticket INC-2026-1792003456 and starting postmortem doc. :thumbsup:

ben-sre: Small note: root cause was a quota tightening that looked OK in canary but scale pattern in prod caused throttling + backend retries -> upstream saturation. We'll add canary traffic shaping for quota tests.

incident-bot: incident closed to P2 at 22:40:20Z.
